canonicalJson.decision: keep the two encoders apart; pin both; do not merge

encoders.lenient: canonicalJson in project-shape-manifest.ts: a total function, drops undefined members, flattens any object, key order is that of Object.fromEntries (array-index keys first, numerically)
encoders.strict: encodeCanonicalJson in polaris-generation-core canonical-json.ts: a validating encoder with limits and failure codes, key order by code unit
encoders.cap1: deterministicLayer in cap1-core evaluation.ts (not exported from the barrel): equal to the lenient one except that it drops an own __proto__ key

suiteWideTap.what: every call to either encoder during the full test suite, spelled by both encoders (strict with generous limits) and compared
suiteWideTap.productionOriginMeans: the first caller frame is production code; the value may still be a test fixture
suiteWideTap.instrumentationFailures: the tapped full run had 3 failing tests, all caused by the instrumentation itself (the no-egress build, the proxy hooks in canonical-json.test.ts that the tap runs, and the live-source closure guard); none by this change

canonicalJson.whyNotMerged: Merging would make the strict encoder refuse the 754 production lenient calls that carry an undefined member or a BigInt (about 52 percent of the 1,433), and would change the digests of every PWB identity. The only value class on which the two disagree without either refusing is the array-index key order (31 of 600 in population B); no production caller was seen to carry one.
